candidates.title: MixPQ: Joint Pruning and Quantization for Speech and Language Foundation Models Compression
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing
candidates.abstract: Large speech and language foundation models are heavily parameterized. This paper introduces MixPQ, a unified framework for the efficient and robust compression of these models. First, we propose a Hessian-aware, layer-wise mixed-sparsity pruning algorithm designed for both language and speech models, yielding promising results even at high sparsity levels. This approach introduces improved saliency criteria for more accurate selection of pruning elements and dynamically assigns different sparsity ratios to weight matrices based on Hessian sensitivity. Second, we present an outlier-aware, column-level mixed-precision quantization framework. This framework introduces a novel quantization sensitivity metric based on the outlier ratio to assess parameter importance and incorporates a mixed outlier reservation strategy to adaptively preserve full-precision outliers across columns in weight matrices, achieving significant performance gains with minimal memory overhead. Experimental results show that our pruning algorithm achieves 2x compression while maintaining performance. And the quantization framework delivers 4-bit lossless compression. In lower-bit scenarios, MixPQ provides an equivalent 2.12-bit model, yielding approximately 16x compression but only with $< $1% WER performance loss in speech recognition. Compared to previous methods, MixPQ demonstrates state-of-the-art performance in various models, particularly at high compression ratios. Moreover, the combination of pruning and quantization can achieve better performance with a higher compression ratio. Finally, the inference analysis highlight MixPQ’s practical benefits in speed and memory efficiency.
candidates.reason: 音声・言語基盤モデル向けに、Hessian感度で層別に疎率を割り当てる構造プルーニングと、外れ値比率に基づく列別混合精度量子化を統合したMixPQを提案し、2倍圧縮でも性能を維持する。プルーニングと量子化の統合圧縮機構であり推論展開への直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: LiM Pruner: Efficient Pruning for Large Language-in-Memory Models
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionized the fields of language understanding and generation, positioning themselves as transformative tools across a wide array of applications as general-purpose task solvers. However, the immense size of LLMs introduces significant challenges for deployment on traditional computing systems, largely due to the inherent von Neumann bottleneck. Recently, Computein-Memory (CiM) architectures have emerged as a groundbreaking solution to accelerate Deep Learning (DL) models, seamlessly integrating computation within the memory fabric to overcome the memory wall bottleneck. While there has been recent progress in mapping generative AIs and LLMs to CiM architectures, the deployment of these models with hundreds of billions of parameters remains very challenging, particularly for edge computing environments. To address the specific challenges of deploying LLMs in memory-centric architectures, we coin the term Language-in-Memory (LiM) to describe a new class of models specifically optimized for such systems. In this context, we present, for the first time, LiM Pruner, a suite of LiM compression techniques specifically designed to induce sparsity in pretrained LLMs. Additionally, we investigate data-path architectures to enhance support for pruned LiM models by addressing potential dislocation challenges. Our comprehensive evaluation of the LiM Pruner on the LLaMA-2 model demonstrates its superior performance compared to traditional pruning techniques.
candidates.reason: メモリ内計算（CiM）アーキテクチャへ数千億パラメータ級LLMを載せる Language-in-Memory という配置形態を定義し、その専用プルーニングであるLiM Prunerでメモリ中心アーキテクチャ向けにモデルを削減する。エッジ推論展開の圧縮機構として直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: ALPS: An Application-Aware, Length-Predictive Scheduler for Efficient LLM Inference at Edge
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
candidates.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) on resource-constrained edge server clusters introduces a critical systems challenge: achieving high throughput and low latency under strict GPU memory and bandwidth limits. Current schedulers are ill-suited for this environment, as they treat requests independently, incurring two major inefficiencies. They waste compute and memory on redundant prefill computations for identical, lengthy system prompts across applications, and their phase-agnostic policies create suboptimal batches that poorly overlap compute-intensive prefills with memory-bound decodes, leading to GPU under-utilization. This paper presents ALPS, an application-aware, length-predictive scheduler for request serving for edge LLM inference. ALPS transforms the queueing layer into an intelligent orchestrator with two core techniques: (i) semantic-aware request grouping, which hashes requests by system prompt to co-locate them, reducing redundant prefill computations; and (ii) phase-aware scheduling, which uses a lightweight output token bucket predictor to estimate decode/prefill ratios and strategically reorders requests to maximize prefill-decode overlap in continuous hybrid batching. Augmented with SLO-aware preemption, ALPS is implemented as a practical scheduling layer atop vLLM. Extensive evaluations on an edge GPU testbed with diverse models and production workloads demonstrate that ALPS improves token throughput by up to 1.6× and reduces end-to-end latency by up to 2.4× compared to state-of-the-art schedulers.
candidates.reason: エッジサーバ群向けに、同一システムプロンプトの冗長プリフィルをハッシュによる意味的グルーピングで削減し、出力長予測バケットでプリフィルとデコードのバッチ編成を分けるALPSスケジューラを提案する。エッジLLMサービングのスケジューリング機構への直接貢献である。
